document.title: Time-Space Tradeoffs and Short Collisions in Merkle-Damgard Hash Functions

candidate.title: The STB Conjecture for Short Collisions in Merkle-Damgard Hashing
candidate.subtitle: Is the length-B preprocessing attack optimal for every block bound?
candidate.one_line: Whether the STB attack is optimal for finding B-block Merkle-Damgard collisions in the auxiliary-input random-oracle model, for every 2 <= B <= T.
candidate.status_note: Settled at B=1 (DGK17), B=2 (the paper's own Theorem 7; simpler proof in AGL22), every constant B (GK22), B ~ T (CDGS18), and every 2 < B < T with ST^2 <= N (AGL22). Open for non-constant B with 2 < B < T and ST^2 > N, where the published bound and the published attack are a factor of up to S apart.
candidate.progress_note: The paper proves the attack (Theorem 3) and the B=2 upper bound (Theorem 7), proves that the bit-fixing route cannot give any length-sensitive bound (Theorem 5), and proves the conjectured upper bound against all zero-walk adversaries up to a ln(NB) factor (Theorem 8).
risks: The printed conjecture attaches no range to B; the range 2 <= B <= T is supplied on the page and flagged in a remark.
The printed Theta is not established even on its lower half (Theorem 3 loses a log N); every later treatment uses Omega-tilde/O-tilde, and the page records the polylogarithmic reading as intended.
The regime description of what remains open comes from GK22 and AGL22, both later than the source, and is attributed to them.

grounding.quote: Concretely, we put forth and study the following conjecture:
The best attack with time T and space S for finding collisions of length B in salted MD hash functions built from hash functions with n-bit outputs achieves success probability

It appears that we could, in principle, obtain similar bounds for other small length bounds like 3 and 4, but these proofs would be too long and complex for us to write down; Going to arbitrary length bounds seems to be out of reach, but there is no inherent obstruction in applying our technique to the general case with new ideas.
We show that the BF-to-AI template inherently cannot give a lower bound for finding short collisions, because finding short collisions in the BF-RO model is relatively easy.
It is tempting to conjecture such an attack is optimal for the bounded case, as it was for the unbounded case, and we are not aware of a better attack.
Our STB conjecture, if true, would explain the non-existence of these attacks
They proved the STB conjecture in the setting B = T , showing an attack with success probability
Merkle-Damgård hashing is defined MDh : [N ] × [M ]+ → [N ] recursively by MDh (a, α) = h(a, α) for α ∈ [M ], and
We say A = (A1 , A2 ) is an (S, T, B)-AI adversary if A1 outputs S bits, A2 issues T queries to its oracle, and the outputs of A2 each consist of B or fewer blocks.

verify.reason: The conjecture is printed, named and genuinely open in the region claimed. Three strength defects in the first draft were repaired: an unrestricted range for B (false at B=1), an assertion that the printed Theta's lower half is proved (Theorem 3 loses a log N), and a claim that the paper gives no account of difficulty (it gives two, Theorems 5 and 8).

checks.finding: Printed as a named, set-off statement on p. 2, introduced on p. 1 by 'we put forth and study the following conjecture'.

Read past p. 2 through all of sections 3-11: the paper proves the attack, the BF barrier, the B=2 case, the need to modify Impagliazzo-Kabanets, and the zero-walk case only. p. 27 still calls the bounded-case optimality a conjecture.

Printed sentence gives no range for B. Unrestricted, the formula is false at B=1, where DGK17 (the paper's [6]) gives Theta(S/N + T^2/N). Corrected to 2 <= B <= T with a remark recording that the range is supplied.

Theorem 3 gives (STB - 96S)/(48 N log N), short of Omega(STB/N) by log N, so the literal Theta is unproved on both halves. Theorem 3 is now reproduced verbatim with its side conditions B <= T < N/4, STB <= N/2, M >= N, and a remark records the polylogarithmic reading.

The conjecture is the harvested paper's own; B=T is attributed to CDGS18, B=1 to DGK17, pre-sampling to Unruh as tightened by CDGS18, concentration to Impagliazzo-Kabanets. GK22 and AGL22 postdate the paper and are flagged.

MD and the auxiliary-input game reproduce the paper's p. 6 definition and Definitions 1-2 on p. 7 clause for clause, including independent uniform h and a, and the (S,T,B) resource convention quoted above.

First draft claimed the paper offers no account of difficulty. Corrected: Theorem 5 (p. 9) proves the bit-fixing route is length-blind, and Theorem 8 (p. 28) proves the conjectured bound against all zero-walk adversaries up to ln(NB). The Hellman-threshold remark is attributed to AGL22, not to the source.
Definitions 1-2 and the notation list fix the quantity, the resource conventions, the asymptotic convention and the open regime.
